topics.caution: The explanation could turn 'ગાયે લીધાં ગાનાં વાછરું રે, અસતરીએ લીધાં નાનાં બાળ' into a rule that child-care is only the woman's place, or read the woman-cow pairing as diminishing rather than as the song's parallel structure (every creature and every household member secures what it loves as the rain comes).
topics.guidance: Explain it as the song's list of who-secures-what before the rain — the ox and farmer take up the yoke and rope, the cow gathers her calf, the mother gathers her children — as one more picture in the same rhythm as the earlier lines, not as a statement about what women's work is; keep the real_life_example open to any family member sheltering someone or something before rain, not narrowed to a mother.
